lifecycle.label: Before
lifecycle.definition: Records already classified as precursors: preparation, training, evaluation, or earlier activity that supplies incident context. This is a role-based lens, not a newly inferred time boundary.

lifecycle.label: During
lifecycle.definition: Records already classified as incident activity or decisions and coordination. This includes attempts, failures, statements, and reported results, with each record retaining its own modality and evidence status.

lifecycle.label: After
lifecycle.definition: Records already classified as response, mitigation, investigation, or aftermath. Response and investigation can overlap ongoing incident activity in calendar time; After does not assert that all intrusion had ended.

stages.label: Artifactory escape
stages.definition: Access, boundary crossing, and related activity grouped around Artifactory; attached records distinguish attempts, reported effects, and response.

stages.label: Evaluation coordination
stages.definition: Requests, evaluation operations, coordination, and related findings kept together in the original mixed evaluation phase.

stages.label: Credential discovery
stages.definition: External-access and credential-discovery activity, including related requests, decisions, and reported results.

stages.label: External staging
stages.definition: Activity around external footholds and staging resources, retaining the source distinction between preparation and effective access.

stages.label: Hugging Face intrusion
stages.definition: The original Hugging Face intrusion phase, including component actions, attempts, coordination, and reported technical effects.

stages.label: Investigation & disclosure
stages.definition: Investigative findings and disclosure-related activity from the mixed original phase; some records retain incident-activity or decision roles.

stages.label: OpenAI compromise
stages.definition: Activity and findings grouped around the compromise of OpenAI internal systems, with system-specific scope retained on each record.

stages.label: Containment & repair
stages.definition: Concrete containment and remediation records, preserving the distinction between an action being taken and evidence that it was effective.

stages.label: Training & evaluation
stages.definition: The original training-and-evaluation precursor phase, including task conditions, restrictions, and earlier reported behavior.

stages.label: Source control & CI
stages.definition: Activity involving source repositories and continuous-integration access; unsuccessful, disputed, and successful effects remain distinct.

stages.label: Sol participation
stages.definition: The original phase describing Sol participation in Hugging Face intrusion activity; this label does not identify every unnamed agent elsewhere.
stages.source_phase: Sol participation in Hugging Face intrusion

stages.label: Supply-chain poisoning
stages.definition: Artifact-poisoning actions and reported downstream findings, without presuming that a modified artifact was consumed or executed.

stages.label: Investigation & repair
stages.definition: The original mixed investigation-and-remediation phase, retaining each record’s existing lifecycle role.

stages.label: External control
stages.definition: External-host activity, foothold attempts, execution, and control as reported in the original phase.

stages.label: Cloud reconnaissance
stages.definition: Cloud-service and credential reconnaissance activity; a probe or attempted access is not evidence of a successful compromise.

stages.label: Database access & review
stages.definition: Internal-database activity and investigative findings kept together in their original mixed phase; individual system scope distinguishes databases.

stages.label: Private Hub attempts
stages.definition: Attempts and supporting activity directed at the private Hub database, preserving authentication and outcome qualifiers.

stages.label: Data staging & transport
stages.definition: Reported preparation, staging, chunking, or transport activity, with the identity and sensitivity of the data limited to what each record states.

stages.label: Agent coordination
stages.definition: Agent communications and coordination records; a message can be a displayable event without proving that its requested action occurred.

stages.label: Termination & access loss
stages.definition: Reported termination and loss of access. The existing records carry incident-activity roles, so they remain in During despite the Response workstream label.

stages.label: Scorer & reset experiments
stages.definition: Experiments and proposals concerning scorer behavior, evaluation targets, or resets, with decisions separated from executed tests.

stages.label: Decisions & restraint
stages.definition: Decisions, restraint, and related investigation recorded in the original phase; narrated intent is not independent proof of motivation or action.

stages.label: Concealment & evasion
stages.definition: Actions and decisions grouped around concealment or evasion, preserving blocked attempts and the limits of any claimed result.

stages.label: Tools & transcripts
stages.definition: Work on tools, transcripts, and related evaluation mechanisms, including assignments and experiments as well as reported modifications.

stages.label: Earlier training
stages.definition: The separate original training-precursor phase. It is retained alongside Training & evaluation rather than merging distinct source groupings.

stages.label: Decisions & recruitment
stages.definition: Recorded decisions to participate or recruit, without treating a stated decision as proof that the subsequent activity took place.

stages.label: Vendor response
stages.definition: Vendor development, validation, remediation, and disclosure records preserved from the original phase.

entity_types.label: Event
entity_types.definition: One displayable source-derived record: action, result, statement, decision, or investigative finding. Some records aggregate actions and are not further divisible from the available evidence.

entity_types.label: Actor
entity_types.definition: The actor phrase attached to a record, with its existing type and model qualifiers. This is an attribution mention, not a newly resolved person, agent instance, or malicious actor identity.
entity_types.identity: Record-scoped mention actor:<event_id>; identical generic phrases are not automatically merged.

entity_types.label: System
entity_types.definition: The normalized system context already recorded in system_scope. A context link can describe an attempted target or investigation and does not by itself establish harm.
entity_types.identity: Exact system_scope value; no additional infrastructure equivalence inferred.

entity_types.label: Lifecycle
entity_types.definition: A Before, During, or After lens derived from the existing incident-role classification, independently of calendar date.

entity_types.label: Stage
entity_types.definition: One of the 27 existing narrative phases, with a shorter display label. A stage is a grouping, not an assertion of temporal order or causal necessity.
entity_types.identity: incident-ontology.json stages[].id; source_phase retains the original label.

entity_types.label: Workstream
entity_types.definition: One of six navigation groups of existing phases. Color identifies this category and does not identify severity, outcome, or evidence quality.

entity_types.label: Source
entity_types.definition: A cited publication in the canonical source catalog. A link identifies the account supporting a record, not independent verification of every claim.

entity_types.label: Assessment
entity_types.definition: The separate, versioned provisional severity assessment for a record, retaining rationale, scope, confidence, and source evidence. It is not a property asserted by the original source.
entity_types.identity: severity-assessments.json records[].id joined to event.id; version supplied by the assessment file.

relation_types.label: Grouped in stage
relation_types.definition: Assigns the record to its original narrative phase. The relation name does not override modality or assert that a proposed action occurred.

relation_types.label: Part of lifecycle
relation_types.definition: Assigns the record’s existing role to Before, During, or After. It does not impose a calendar ordering on records.

relation_types.label: Part of workstream
relation_types.definition: Groups an unchanged source phase into one of the six display workstreams.

relation_types.label: Attributed to actor
relation_types.definition: Carries the record’s existing actor attribution. For statements, decisions, observations, or failed attempts, it attributes that recorded modality rather than inventing an executed action.
relation_types.binding: event.id -> record-scoped actor mention from event.actor, event.actor_type, event.actor_model
relation_types.cardinality: one record-scoped mention per event; a phrase may name a group

relation_types.label: Concerns system
relation_types.definition: Connects the record to its recorded system context. This neutral association applies to attempts, findings, coordination, and actions without implying a realized effect.
relation_types.cardinality: one recorded system-context phrase per event

relation_types.label: Reported effect on system
relation_types.definition: An optional qualified effect relation for a positively assessed reported technical effect within the record’s stated system context. It must retain the assessment scope and source evidence status; it is never generated from a stage label or an attempted action alone.
relation_types.binding: event.id -> exact event.system_scope only when its current assessment has outcome=adverse and score in 1..5; attach assessment.rationale, assessment.scope, event.modality and event.epistemic_status.
relation_types.cardinality: zero or one qualified relation per event

relation_types.label: Supported by source
relation_types.definition: Preserves the primary citation and locator for the record. Additional source locators remain attached exactly as stored and are not resolved into invented citations.
relation_types.binding: event.id -> event.source_id, retaining event.source_locator, event.source_url and event.additional_source_locators
relation_types.cardinality: one canonical primary-source link per event

relation_types.label: Assessed as
relation_types.definition: Joins the event to its current separate analyst assessment, including explicit unassessed and intentionally unnumbered categories. Canonical observed_severity is retained as archival data.
relation_types.binding: event.id -> severity-assessments.records[].id using exact ID equality
relation_types.cardinality: one current assessment entry per event

facets.label: Lifecycle
facets.definition: Role-based Before, During, and After membership.

facets.label: Stage
facets.definition: The original narrative phase under a shorter display label.

facets.label: Actor
facets.definition: Source-derived actor phrase, type, and supported model name.

facets.label: System
facets.definition: Recorded system context and target wording.

facets.label: Evidence
facets.definition: Reported, reasoning, inferred, or differing accounts, retaining the original evidence qualifiers.

facets.label: Time
facets.definition: Reported dates, individual times, and bounded source-context intervals. A layout coordinate is not new temporal evidence.

facets.label: Severity
facets.definition: The separate current analyst assessment; positional and textual, independent of workstream color.

facets.label: Source
facets.definition: Publication and locator supporting the event record.

provenance.standards_use: STIX 2.1 informs typed entity relationships and explicit contextual grouping. CASE/UCO informs separate object descriptions, qualified relationships, and traceability from sources to analysis. These are conceptual influences; this local JSON ontology is not a STIX bundle, CASE/UCO serialization, compliance claim, or external endorsement.
provenance.relation_materialization: Event-to-lifecycle and event-to-stage membership are materialized in assignments; stage-to-workstream membership is materialized in stages. The remaining relation types are explicit field bindings into the canonical dataset and current assessment sidecar, not newly asserted event-to-event links.
provenance.classification_status: Provisional analyst navigation ontology derived from an existing provisional event inventory.

scopes.lifecycle: Before, During, and After classify incident roles, not mutually exclusive time windows. An After response may overlap a During intrusion on the calendar.
scopes.stage: Each stage preserves exactly one original phase. A stage can contain records from several lifecycle views; no stage is forced into only one lifecycle.
scopes.workstream: Workstream and lifecycle are independent facets. For example, Termination & access loss belongs to the Response workstream but its five canonical incident-activity records remain in During.
scopes.mixed_phases: Mixed source labels are not split by guesswork. Database access & review remains in Intrusion and includes both activity and investigative findings. Investigation & disclosure contains both During and After records.
scopes.actor_identity: Actor phrases are record-scoped mentions. Repeated Agent or Agents labels do not establish identical identities, distinct agents, or a shared model.
scopes.system_effect: System context is available for every record. A reported-effect link requires a qualifying current assessment; failed requests, intent, and investigation alone do not establish an adverse system effect.
scopes.evidence: Source-reported occurrence is not independent verification. Reasoning, inference, conflicting accounts, uncertainty, and source granularity remain attached to the original event.
scopes.time: Chronological display, interval placement, and animated movement supply navigation. They establish neither an exact event time nor a causal relation.
scopes.causality: No causes, enables, prevents, or precedes relation is inferred between events. Shared stage, source passage, actor wording, and temporal proximity do not establish causation.
scopes.assessment: Current severity remains a separate provisional organizational-consequence judgment. The whole-incident assessment is not automatically inherited by individual records.
scopes.inventory: 832 is the current displayable inventory, not a proven maximum of real-world actions. Grouped source accounts cannot be split further without additional evidence.

glossary.definition: A local model defining the kinds of things in the incident dataset, their properties, and the relationships that can be justified between them.
One displayable record with attached evidence. It can describe an action, attempt, result, statement, decision, or finding.
Separated into the smallest supported displayable units available in the reviewed material. This does not create missing per-agent actions or inaccessible log entries.
The Before, During, or After role-based lens. It is separate from an event’s date.
A detailed narrative grouping corresponding exactly to one existing phase label.
A broad categorical grouping of stages used for navigation and color.
An independent way to inspect the same event, such as stage, actor, evidence, time, or severity. Haruspex facets are local display concepts, not UCO Facet instances.
A named connection with an explicit source, target, and evidential meaning. Membership and source attribution do not imply causation.
The retained path from a cited source and locator through the canonical record to a later classification or assessment.

sources.locator: Sections 1.2.1 Graph-Based Model, 4.4 Grouping, and 5.1 Relationship
sources.use: Grounds the distinction between typed nodes, named relationships, and explicitly contextual groupings. Haruspex uses those design ideas without adopting STIX object types or claiming valid STIX serialization.

sources.title: CASE Ontology Design and Specification
sources.locator: Sections 2.3.1 Facet and Observable Object, 2.3.3 Relationships, 3.2 Provenance, and 6.2 InvestigativeAction and Role
sources.use: Grounds explicit descriptions, contextual roles, qualified relationships, and preservation of links between source material and analysis. Haruspex retains these distinctions without claiming CASE/UCO conformance or a forensic chain of custody.
